'''Bice Sechi-Zorn''' (1928 – 10 December 1984, Hamburg<ref>physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/pdf/10.1063/1.2814543</ref>) was an Italian/American nuclear [[physicist]], and professor at the [[University of Maryland]].

==Life==
She graduated from [[University of Cagliari]].  She met her husband, [[Gus T. Zorn]], at the [[University of Padua]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.physics.umd.edu/announcements/zorn.html |title=Dr. Gus T. Zorn |publisher=University of Maryland Department of Physics |date=2002-01-30 |access-date=2014-06-10}}</ref> They both worked at the University of Maryland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencephoto.com/media/574599/view |title=Bice Sechi-Zorn, Italian-US physicist |publisher=Science Photo Library |date= |access-date=2014-06-10}}</ref>
She was a professor of physics beginning from 1976 to 1984.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.physics.ucla.edu/~cwp/Phase2/Sechi-Zorn,_Bice@853449324.html |title=Bice Sechi-Zorn |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=101 |journal=Contributions of 20th Century Women to Physics |access-date=2014-06-10 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220053245/http://www.physics.ucla.edu/~cwp/Phase2/Sechi-Zorn%2C_Bice%40853449324.html |archive-date=2014-12-20 |bibcode=1985PhT....38d.101G |last1=Glasser |first1=Robert G. |last2=Snow |first2=George A. |year=1985 |doi=10.1063/1.2814543 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

A Gus T. Zorn and Bice Sechi-Zorn Professorship in Experimental Physics is named for her.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.urhome.umd.edu/CPMAG/summer02/profiles.html |title=maryland live... |work=College Park Magazine |publisher=University of Maryland |date=2002-01-30 |access-date=2014-06-10 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111211046/http://www.urhome.umd.edu/CPMAG/summer02/profiles.html |archive-date=2014-11-11 }}</ref>
